subject: Numeracy
title: One for you, one for me
objectives: Children will give one object to each friend.
Children will show when there is not enough with support.
content: One-to-one correspondence in sharing: giving one object to each friend and noticing when there is not enough.
teachingActivities: Model "one for you, one for me" slowly; use real friends and toys; ask "Does everyone have one?" and let children check.
learnerActivities: Hand out one object to each friend, check that everyone has one, and notice who has none.
assessment: Check whether each child gives one object to each of up to four friends and notices when someone has none.
expectedOutcomes: Hands out one object to each of up to four friends.

lessons.title: One for you, one for me
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Children will give one object to a friend and keep one for themselves.
successCriteria: Gives one object to a friend
Says "one for you" or "one for me"
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can give one to a friend, count to five with support and use more and same.
lessons.starter: Hold two biscuits and say "One for you, one for me!" Give one to the soft toy and keep one. Say "We both have one."
teacherActivities: Share four biscuits between yourself and the soft toy, saying "one for you, one for me" each time.
Ask "Do we both have the same?" and count the biscuits on each plate.
Invite a child to share with a friend using two biscuits.
learnerActivities: Children watch and say the sentence with you.
Children count and say "same".
Child gives one biscuit to the friend and keeps one.
Each child shares with a new partner.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Share four biscuits between yourself and the soft toy, saying "one for you, one for me" each time. Children: Children watch and say the sentence with you.
Step 2. Teacher: Ask "Do we both have the same?" and count the biscuits on each plate. Children: Children count and say "same".
Step 3. Teacher: Invite a child to share with a friend using two biscuits. Children: Child gives one biscuit to the friend and keeps one.
Step 4. Teacher: Swap partners and repeat. Children: Each child shares with a new partner.

practical.title: Sharing pairs
steps: Give each pair a plate with two toy biscuits.
Share one each and say the sentence.
practical.safety: Use toy biscuits larger than a child’s fist. If using real food, wash hands and check allergies first.

differentiation.support: Use two biscuits and model the sharing hand-over-hand.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to share six biscuits between two friends.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: What do we say when we share?
questions.expected: One for you, one for me.

lessons.conclusion: Hold up the plates and say "One for you, one for me. We share."
lessons.homeConnection: Share a snack with a sibling using one for you and one for me.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "give one object to a friend and keep one for themselves" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

learnerFacing.songOrRhyme: One for you, one for me, one for you, one for me. Sharing is kind, sharing is fun.

lessons.title: Everyone has one
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Children will give out one cup to each friend at a table.
successCriteria: Gives one cup to each friend
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can give one to a friend, count to five with support and use more and same.
resources: Four soft toys seated around a mat
lessons.starter: Seat four soft toys around the mat. Say "The toys are thirsty. Each toy needs one cup. Let us give out the cups."
teacherActivities: Give one cup to the first toy and say "one cup for Teddy".
Ask a child to give a cup to the next toy. Continue around the circle.
Ask "Does every toy have one cup?" and check each toy.
Remove one cup and ask "Who has no cup?"
learnerActivities: Children say "one" and watch.
Child gives one cup to each toy.
Children point to each toy and say "yes" or "no".
Children point to the toy without a cup.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Give one cup to the first toy and say "one cup for Teddy". Children: Children say "one" and watch.
Step 2. Teacher: Ask a child to give a cup to the next toy. Continue around the circle. Children: Child gives one cup to each toy.
Step 3. Teacher: Ask "Does every toy have one cup?" and check each toy. Children: Children point to each toy and say "yes" or "no".
Step 4. Teacher: Remove one cup and ask "Who has no cup?" Children: Children point to the toy without a cup.

practical.title: Cups for the toys
steps: Seat the toys in a circle.
Give one cup to each toy.
Check that every toy has one.
practical.safety: Use unbreakable plastic cups; children walk carefully around the circle.

differentiation.support: Use two toys and two cups.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to give out cups to five toys.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: Does every toy have a cup?
questions.expected: Yes when every toy has one.

lessons.conclusion: Collect the cups one by one and say "Thank you, toys."
lessons.homeConnection: When setting the table, give one plate and one cup to each person.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "give out one cup to each friend at a table" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Enough or not enough?
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Children will check whether there is enough for everyone and say when there is not enough.
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can give one to a friend, count to five with support and use more and same.
resources: Four soft toys or children as guests
lessons.starter: Show a basket with only three fruits and four toys. Say "Oh no! There are four toys but only three fruits. Is there enough?"
teacherActivities: Give one fruit to each toy and stop when the fruit runs out. Say "Teddy has none."
Ask "How can we fix it?" and add one more fruit.
Try with different numbers of fruits and toys.
Say "Enough!" when each toy has one.
learnerActivities: Children point to the toy with no fruit.
Children say "more" or give the extra fruit.
Children give one fruit to each toy and check.
Children say "enough" and clap.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Give one fruit to each toy and stop when the fruit runs out. Say "Teddy has none." Children: Children point to the toy with no fruit.
Step 2. Teacher: Ask "How can we fix it?" and add one more fruit. Children: Children say "more" or give the extra fruit.
Step 3. Teacher: Try with different numbers of fruits and toys. Children: Children give one fruit to each toy and check.
Step 4. Teacher: Say "Enough!" when each toy has one. Children: Children say "enough" and clap.

practical.title: Enough for everyone
steps: Give each group four toys and a basket of fruits.
Give one fruit to each toy.
Say if there is enough or if more are needed.
practical.safety: Use large toy fruits; keep baskets on the table; supervise group play.

differentiation.support: Use two toys and two fruits, and point out when each has one.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to count how many more fruits are needed.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: Does everyone have a fruit?
questions.expected: Yes or no, with a gesture.

expectedOutcomes: Notices when there is not enough
Asks for or gives one more
lessons.conclusion: Put the extra fruit in the basket and say "Enough for everyone."
lessons.homeConnection: Count whether there is enough chairs for everyone at the table.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "check whether there is enough for everyone and say when there is not enough" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Party for friends
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Children will plan a pretend party and share one item with each guest.
successCriteria: Gives one item to each guest
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can give one to a friend, count to five with support and use more and same.
lessons.starter: Spread a party cloth. Say "We are having a party for our toy friends! Let us make sure every friend gets one plate, one cup and one biscuit."
teacherActivities: Place a plate in front of each toy and say "one plate each".
Place a cup on each plate and say "one cup each".
Give one biscuit to each guest and say "one biscuit each".
Sing a party song and clap as each guest is served.
learnerActivities: Children place one plate for each guest.
Children place one cup on each plate.
Children give out the biscuits and say "one for you".
Children clap and sing.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Place a plate in front of each toy and say "one plate each". Children: Children place one plate for each guest.
Step 2. Teacher: Place a cup on each plate and say "one cup each". Children: Children place one cup on each plate.
Step 3. Teacher: Give one biscuit to each guest and say "one biscuit each". Children: Children give out the biscuits and say "one for you".
Step 4. Teacher: Sing a party song and clap as each guest is served. Children: Children clap and sing.

practical.title: Toy party
steps: Seat soft toys around the cloth.
Give each toy a plate, a cup and a biscuit.
practical.safety: Use toy food and unbreakable plates; children walk carefully; wash hands after play.

differentiation.support: Serve only two guests with one item each.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to give out items to five guests and count them.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: How many plates for four guests?

expectedOutcomes: Shares one item with each guest
lessons.conclusion: Say "Thank you" to each guest and clear the party cloth together.
lessons.homeConnection: Help to set the table for a family meal with one item for each person.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "plan a pretend party and share one item with each guest" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

boardContent: One plate, one cup, one biscuit

lessons.title: Sharing stations
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Children will show they can share one each at three stations.
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can give one to a friend, count to five with support and use more and same.
lessons.starter: Sing the sharing song and show the three stations.
teacherActivities: Rotate groups every four minutes and observe one station closely.
Ask "Does everyone have one?" and "Who needs more?"
Record each child’s level and take photographs.
learnerActivities: Children play at each station.
Child checks and answers.
Children tidy at the signal.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Rotate groups every four minutes and observe one station closely. Children: Children play at each station.
Step 2. Teacher: Ask "Does everyone have one?" and "Who needs more?" Children: Child checks and answers.
Step 3. Teacher: Record each child’s level and take photographs. Children: Children tidy at the signal.

practical.title: Station circuit
practical.safety: Use toy items only; supervise stations; keep floors clear.

differentiation.extension: Ask a confident child to show a friend how to share fairly.

assessment.method: Observe and record Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding for: gives one to each of up to four friends; checks that everyone has one; notices when there is not enough.

questions.question: Does everyone have one?
questions.expected: Yes or no, with a gesture.

questions.question: Can you share these with a friend?

expectedOutcomes: Has an observation record for Week 5
Shares one each with growing accuracy
lessons.conclusion: Sing the sharing song and tidy up together.
lessons.homeConnection: Practise one for you, one for me at mealtimes.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "show they can share one each at three stations" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?
